claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks (>12) and claimant is not regularly spending money on child
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.reason: Child in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks (>12) and claimant is not regularly spending money on child

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by initializing the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the age of the child/children you're claiming for:**

Are the children you want to claim Child Benefit for:
- **Under 16 years old?**
- **Between 16 and 19 years old?**
- **20 years old or over?**

Please tell me the age category that applies to your child/children. If you have multiple children in different age groups, we can work through each one. It would be helpful if you could also provide their name(s) so I can track the assessment properly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 8 years old, which means he falls into the **under 16 category** - this is great news as children under 16 automatically qualify as "qualifying children" for Child Benefit purposes.

Now let me navigate to the next stage of the assessment to continue checking your eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, we're moving forward! Here's the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

Given that Alex is 8 years old, I would assume he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just 8, so he's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, so he's definitely not in paid work. Let me continue with the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Here's the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, I need to know: Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits directly in his own name:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Again, given that Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I would expect the answer is "no" (he's not receiving these), but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right. Let me continue to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Here's the next question:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship (or if he were, is it an approved type)?**

Given Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I'm confident he's not in any apprenticeship at all. Can you confirm:
- Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?

If not, we can move straight ahead. If he is, I'd need to know which country (England, Scotland, or Wales) and what type of apprenticeship.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's only 8, so he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - Alex is not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we've reached a key eligibility check - **residency requirements**.

This is a multi-path check, which means if **ANY** of the following apply to you, you can proceed:

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status and are working** (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 months)
4. **You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work** (jobseeker for up to 91 days)
5. **You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources** (and not claiming Income Support, JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)
6. **You have pre-settled status as a student** (with sufficient resources)
7. **You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national** (spouse, dependent child under 21, or dependent parent)
8. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** (in certain qualifying countries)

**Can you tell me which of these situations applies to you?** The most common one is simply that you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK. Let me move to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check if you're responsible for Alex. This is another multi-path check - if **ANY** of the following applies, you can proceed:

1. **You live with the child** - You live with Alex
2. **You're contributing to the child's upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (or in kind) towards their care, including food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.
3. **You're paying maintenance under court order or agreement** - You make maintenance payments towards Alex's upkeep that equal or exceed the Child Benefit payment

**Which of these applies to you?** Given the context, I assume you live with Alex in Manchester, but please confirm your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - you live with Alex in Manchester. Let me move to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

**Is there anyone else (for example, Alex's other parent, another family member, or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or who might also be eligible to claim for him?**

The possible situations are:
- **No one else is claiming** - You're the only person claiming for Alex
- **Someone else is claiming, but you've agreed who should claim** - You've discussed it and agreed one of you should claim
- **Someone else is claiming and there's a dispute** - You're not sure who should be claiming, or you disagree

Which situation applies?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me move to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation to see if any special rules apply.

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **In hospital** - Is Alex currently in hospital?
- **In care** - Is Alex in local authority care?
- **Fostered** - Is Alex being fostered?
- **Normal living** - Is Alex living at home with you (normal circumstances)?

Based on what you've told me so far, I'd assume Alex is living at home with you normally, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has been in hospital for a few months now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I'm sorry to hear Alex has been in hospital. This is an important detail as there are specific rules about Child Benefit when a child is in hospital.

Let me get the specific rules about hospital duration to understand your situation better.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand Alex's hospital situation better, as there are specific rules about how long a child can be in hospital while you still claim Child Benefit.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **How long has Alex been in hospital?** (You mentioned "a few months" - is it been more than 12 weeks/about 3 months?)

2. **Has there been any gap or break in his hospital stay?** For example, has he come home for visits or breaks, or has it been continuous?

The key detail is that normally Child Benefit can continue for up to **12 weeks** while a child is in hospital. However, there's a special rule: if a child comes home for breaks of less than 28 days, the time in hospital is "linked" and counts as continuous.

Let me navigate to the hospital duration check so I can ask you the right questions.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I have the detailed rules. Let me ask you the specific questions about Alex's hospital stay:

**About Alex's hospital stay:**

1. **How long has Alex been in hospital in total?** Please count all the time - if he's had multiple stays, add them all together. Has it been:
   - Less than 12 weeks total?
   - More than 12 weeks total?

2. **If Alex has had breaks at home between hospital stays, how long were those breaks?** Were they:
   - Less than 28 days between stays?
   - More than 28 days between stays?

(If breaks were less than 28 days, all the hospital time counts towards the 12-week limit. If breaks were 28+ days, the counter resets.)

Please give me as much detail as you can about the timeline of Alex's hospital stay(s).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital continuously - no breaks home at all. It's been about 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarity. So Alex has been in hospital continuously for about 15 weeks with no breaks at home.

This is important information. The rule is that Child Benefit can normally continue for up to **12 weeks** while a child is in hospital. Since Alex has now been in hospital for **15 weeks continuously**, he has exceeded that 12-week limit.

However, let me check the next question in the assessment, as there may be additional circumstances that could allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit even beyond the 12-week limit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! There's an important exception. Even though Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you may still be eligible if you meet this condition:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?**

This could include expenses such as:
- Travel to visit him
- Meals when you visit
- Clothes or personal items for him
- Entertainment or activities
- Toiletries
- Other regular contributions towards his care

Your spending counts if you're regularly (not just occasionally) paying for these things. If you're married or in a civil partnership and living together, your partner's spending also counts.

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been able to afford to spend money on his needs while he's in there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's a difficult situation. Unfortunately, since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks and you're not regularly spending money on his needs while he's there, this means you would not be eligible to continue receiving Child Benefit under the current rules.

However, let me continue through the assessment to make sure I've checked all the relevant factors before giving you my final decision. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've reached the final outcome of the assessment. Based on the information you've provided, I need to give you the result:

---

## **INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit - Alex**

### **Reason:**
Child Benefit eligibility stops after a child has been in hospital or residential accommodation for more than **12 weeks**, unless you are regularly spending money on the child during their hospital stay.

In your case:
- **Alex has been in hospital for approximately 15 weeks** (continuously, with no breaks)
- **You are not regularly spending money on Alex's needs** while he's in hospital

### **Important Information:**
The 12-week limit is a key rule in Child Benefit eligibility. However, there are some nuances:
- If Alex were to come home for any period, and then return to hospital within 28 days, the hospital time would be "linked" and count as continuous
- If Alex's situation changes and you begin regularly spending money on his needs, this could potentially change the outcome
- **Partner's spending only counts if you're married or in a civil partnership and living together**

### **Next Steps:**
I recommend you:
1. **Contact HMRC directly** on 0300 200 3100 to discuss your specific circumstances - they may be able to advise on any exceptions or support available
2. **Check if there are other benefits** you might be eligible for to help support Alex during his hospital stay
3. **Keep records** of any spending you do make on Alex's behalf, in case circumstances change

---

Let me now formally record this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm very sorry to hear that you're ineligible for Child Benefit at this time, especially given the challenging circumstances with Alex being in hospital for an extended period. 

However, I do want to emphasize:
- **Please contact HMRC** (0300 200 3100) to discuss your specific situation - they may have guidance on exceptional circumstances
- **If your financial situation changes** and you're able to start regularly spending money on Alex's needs, you may become eligible again
- **Look into other forms of support** that may be available to help during this difficult time

I hope Alex's recovery goes well, and that your circumstances improve soon.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and meets the qualifying child criteria (under 16). He is not in paid work, does not receive benefits in his own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. The claimant lives in the UK (Manchester), lives with Alex, and is the only person claiming for him. However, Alex has been in hospital continuously for approximately 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit for Child Benefit eligibility during hospital stays. The claimant is not regularly spending money on Alex's needs while he is in hospital. Under the rules, Child Benefit stops after 12 weeks in hospital unless the claimant regularly spends money on the child. Therefore, Alex is ineligible.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is seeking Child Benefit for their 8-year-old son Alex, who is currently in hospital. While Alex meets all the standard qualifying criteria (age under 16, living with the claimant, no other claimants, claimant is UK resident), the assessment has identified that Alex has been in continuous hospital accommodation for approximately 15 weeks. This exceeds the 12-week limit for Child Benefit eligibility during hospital stays. As the claimant is not regularly spending money on Alex's needs during his hospital stay, they do not qualify for the exception to this rule. Consequently, the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex under current circumstances."
